neighbours.label: a clause about an unspecified, generic entity ('things', 'everything', 'whatever', 'something'): the generic word itself or the verb after it, as against the same clause shapes with a specific noun
fire: My grandfather says there are more things to worry about than the weather.
She soon realised that something odd was going on in the office.
The guide explains everything there is to see in the old town.
In this house, whatever is broken gets fixed by Dad.
We talked about the things that matter most to us.
He believed that better things were waiting for him in the city.
The course covers everything that must be known before the exam.
Honestly, there are worse things than missing a train.
quiet: My grandfather says there are more clouds today than yesterday.
She soon realised that the printer was broken in the office.
The guide explains the history of the old town.
In this house, the broken chair gets fixed by Dad.
We talked about the teachers who helped us most.
He believed that his brother was waiting for him in the city.
The course covers the chapters assigned before the exam.
Honestly, the train was only ten minutes late.
